title: Расспросы Кости о слабостях Ильи  (Questioning Kostya About Ilya's Weaknesses)

segments.t: Pretending that he wants to bury the hatchet with Ilya, Max casually asks Kostya what kind of things his old friend loves most. Trusting his roommate completely, Kostya gives Max the exact information he needs to prepare a cruel surprise for Ilya.
Не знаю, как к нему подойти, чтобы помириться.
А ты что, реально хочешь с ним помириться?
Слушай, что он любит вообще, а?
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
Не знаю, как к нему подойти, чтобы помириться.
'I do not know how to approach him to make peace.' Notice how Russian expresses 'not' and 'to make peace' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Ilya answers right away.
'Maybe I should invite him out for a beer, huh?' The grammar packs 'maybe' and 'and' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Well, maybe.' Kostya brings out the contrast between 'come on' and 'maybe' in a few short words.
А ты что, реально хочешь с ним помириться?
'Wait, do you seriously want to make peace with him?' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'to make peace' without extra filler words. Kostya answers right away.
'Well yeah, that is why I am asking you.' Notice how Russian expresses 'come on' and 'am asking' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Слушай, что он любит вообще, а?
'Listen, what does he like in general?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'listen' before landing on 'and'.
'Oh, he likes all kinds of things.' In Russian, the idea of 'yes' flows naturally into 'loves' without extra filler words. Ilya answers right away.
'Actually, this will be even better.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'like this' before landing on 'better'.
'He is going to love this.' Kostya anchors the line on 'to him', while 'will please' completes the thought.
'You are welcome.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'not' and finishing on 'what'. Kostya answers right away.
'Thanks, Kostyan.' Kostya brings out the contrast between 'thank you' and 'Kostyan' in a few short words.
'Alright, I am off.' Ilya brings out the contrast between 'let's' and 'I' in a few short words.
'Just a little token.' Notice how Russian expresses 'but' and 'like this' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
Не знаю, как к нему подойти, чтобы помириться.
А ты что, реально хочешь с ним помириться?
Слушай, что он любит вообще, а?
That wraps up this scene as pretending he wants to make peace with Ilya, Max tricks Kostya into telling him what Ilya cares about most so he can strike where it hurts. See you next time!
